notes:
VERDICT: BLOCKED, at the shallowest possible point - the declared request contract does not describe a body the backing service will accept, and the MCP tool's own schema validation prevents sending the body the service actually wants. Never diffed against the declared success schema because no 200 was ever reached; this is a request-shape defect, not a response defect.

WHAT HAPPENED: describeCapability declares exactly one source-tag field, 'source_id' (integer, singular) - 'the tag that LOSES'. Every call using that exact declared field, with the exact declared type (integer, attempt 1) and even coerced to an array (attempt 3), was rejected by the backing service with 400 {"type":"invalid","message":"source_ids is required."}. The backend's own error message names the field it wants: 'source_ids', plural. When attempt 2 tried sending that literal field name as an array (the shape 'source_ids: [541126]' its own error message implies), the request never left the client - the invokeCapability tool rejected it before any HTTP call, because its schema (taken from describeCapability) only whitelists 'entity_type, source_id, target_id' as body keys. So: the declared contract's field name for the losing tag is wrong (should be plural, and very likely accepts multiple source tags at once - a materially different capability shape than 'merge exactly one tag into another'), and the MCP layer's strict enforcement of that wrong declared name makes the correct call unreachable through this tool. This is not a preprod outage or a v1/v2 hang: list_tags_v3 and edit_test_case_partial_v1 both succeeded cleanly against the same project immediately before and after these attempts, and none of the three failures carry the 'the product could not be reached'/status:0 signature - all three are real, addressable 400s or client-side rejections.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE CAPABILITY'S ACTUAL SHAPE: the backend error message 'source_ids is required' (plural) strongly suggests merge_tags_v1's real backing route takes a LIST of source tag ids to merge into one target, not a single source_id as documented - i.e. bulk-merge-many-into-one, not merge-one-into-one. This could not be confirmed further within the 3-attempt budget/tool constraints, but it is the most likely explanation and should route to whoever owns the capability-index entry: rename source_id -> source_ids (array) in the declared contract, and re-test whether entity_type validation, the admin-gate-skipped-outside-prod note, and the 'no envelope, raw passthrough' response-shape guidance still hold once the correct field name is used.

MERGE SEMANTICS QUESTION (does the tag disappear / do cases get repointed / duplicate-vs-single-tag on a case that carried both) - UNVERIFIED. The merge itself never executed, so none of the three questions in the task brief (does the losing tag disappear entirely, do cases carrying it get repointed at the winner, does a case carrying both end up with one tag or a duplicate) could be answered. TC-54486 (1985020) currently still carries BOTH __mcp-probe-mergetag-20260922-a (id 541125, target/would-be-survivor) and __mcp-probe-mergetag-20260922-b (id 541126, source/would-be-loser) - unmerged. Both tags remain live in the project's test_case tag vocabulary (usage_count 1 each) for whoever picks this back up once the contract is fixed, or for a follow-up probe using the corrected 'source_ids' field name (assuming a future MCP-layer redeploy widens the accepted body keys to match).

CLEANUP LEDGER: created __mcp-probe-mergetag-20260922-a (tag id 541125) and __mcp-probe-mergetag-20260922-b (tag id 541126), both attached only to TC-54486 (internal id 1985020, folder 764138, PR-2005/project 379335744). Calling list_tags_v3 with query.search='__mcp-probe-mergetag' returned the full, unfiltered 211-tag list (identical count and identical page-1 contents to an unfiltered call) rather than narrowing to matching names - confirmed by paging p=1..3 with and without the search term and comparing counts/contents. Also: the declared 200 schema promises a top-level 'tags' array; the actual key returned on every call in this session was 'tag_objects', not 'tags' - a renamed-field response drift on the one read capability that did work, noted here since it was encountered en route to the blocked write and is not yet filed elsewhere for this capability.
